data.gender_notes: Arjit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Arjit is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘arhajit’, which means ‘conquering’, ‘victorious’. This name is associated with the god Indra, who is known as the god of war, rain, and thunder. Arjit is a name of great strength and courage, and is believed to bring success and victory in all endeavors. The name Arjit carries the meaning “Conquering, Victorious” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arjit usually hope their child will grow to embody conquering, victorious and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Reference: Mahabharata, Chapter 13, Section 27.
historical_references.context:
Arjit is the name of the king of Hastinapur who was defeated by Bhishma in battle.
Arjit was a grandson of King Yudhishthira, and was removed from the throne by Bhishma.

historical_references.reference:
Arjit is also mentioned in the Puranic literature, particularly in the Brahma Purana, as the name of a deity.
Reference: Brahma Purana, Chapter 111, Verse 19.

Arjit is also known as the god of war and is invoked for success in military endeavors.
